headline: Record quarterly profit caps a strong fiscal year
summary_short: Fourth-quarter revenue rose to $2.34B (+10.8% y/y) and Total Segment EBITDA jumped to $423M (+31.4% y/y), while EPS from continuing operations climbed to $0.33 from $0.16 the prior quarter.
summary_long: Growth was led by Digital Real Estate Services (+19%), Book Publishing (+15%) and Dow Jones (+7%), with REA Group and Move both posting double-digit revenue gains and Dow Jones subscriptions up 7% to 6.7 million. Adjusted EPS was $0.35 versus $0.19 a year ago. Net income attributable to stockholders was $179M, up from $89M last quarter; the year-ago comparable of $743M/$1.31 EPS included a one-time discontinued-operations gain not present this quarter, so that comparison isn't like-for-like. Cash fell to $2.10B from $2.40B a year earlier after $641M of share buybacks (vs $150M prior year) and $204M of dividends paid. The company declared a $0.10/share semi-annual dividend; no numeric forward guidance was issued.

drivers.explanation: Growth driven by higher real estate revenues at Digital Real Estate Services, higher book sales at Book Publishing, and higher circulation/subscription and digital advertising revenue at Dow Jones.
EBITDA growth mirrors the revenue gains across segments, led by Digital Real Estate Services and Dow Jones, partly offset by higher employee and technology costs.
Tracks the rise in net income from continuing operations; the release attributes the year-over-year profit jump to higher Total Segment EBITDA and lower impairment/restructuring charges.

Per the release, continuing-operations net income rose on higher Total Segment EBITDA and lower impairment and restructuring charges versus the prior year; noncontrolling interests take $51M of the $230M continuing-ops total.
Not a company-disclosed line; derived as revenue less operating expenses, SG&A and D&A, which grew because segment revenue growth outpaced cost growth.
Cash declined despite higher free cash flow, as $641M of News Corp share buybacks (vs $150M a year ago), $141M of REA Group share buybacks and $204M of dividends paid outweighed the FCF gain.
CEO Robert Thomson called it an exceptional quarter, crediting Digital Real Estate Services, Dow Jones and Book Publishing as the company's core growth engines behind record profitability.
